topics.title: Art - Meaning, Origin and Uses of Art Primary 5 (Basic 5) - Cultural and Creative Arts
topics.content:
CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ART
FIRST TERM
WEEK 1
PRIMARY 5
THEME: ARTS AND CRAFTS
PREVIOUS LESSON -Third Term Cultural and Creative Arts Plan Lesson Notes for Primary 4 (Basic 4)
TOPIC - ARTS
LEARNING AREA
1. Meaning of Art
2. Uses of Art
3. Origin of Art
4. Branches of Art
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. explain the meaning
2. uses and origin of Arts;
3. name some Nigerian Art works;
4. name the branches of Art.
ENTRY BEHAVIOR
The pupils can identify different art works.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of Illustration of Art Works, Printed materials, Books, Old calendars, Photographs, Charts, Works of Art, Cardboard, Pencil
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
Scheme of Work
9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
Course Book - Fundamentals of Cultural and Creative Art Book 4
All Relevant Material
Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Art is a a visual and non visual presentation of feelings (thoughts) or imagination through drawing, painting, music, drama, literature, dance, etc.
MEANING OF ARTS
Art is the ability to create something beautiful for our use.
ORIGIN OF ART
Art originated from the attempt of man to create from his ideas, items he can use to make life easier and comfortable for himself, his family and community.
The origin of art dates back to the old stone - age when early men used their creativity to produce simple farm implements or tools like cutlasses, hoes and spears. These assisted them in their daily activities of hunting and gathering of crops for their families.
The early men started the art of painting when they documented their hunting experiences on the walls of caves. They also made use of colours from soil and plants to create designs and drawings on the walls of their caves.
Reference - CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ARTS
for Primary Schools 4
A K Badaru, C Ndubuisi, G Akinsola, A Abdul, S A Akinsowo, A Oni.
LESSON 2 - INTRODUCTION
Art is the ability to create something beautiful for our use.
Art originated from the attempt of man to create from his ideas, items he can use to make life easier and comfortable for himself, his family and community.
USES OF ART
Art is created serve many purposes, among these are:
1. It is used for communication.
2. It is used for expressing one’s feelings.
3. It is used for decoration and beautification.
4. It is used for commemoration.
5. It is used for keeping records of important events, history and culture.
6. It used used for worship and ritual.
NIGERIAN ART WORKS
1. Weaving
2. Brass works
3. Pottery
4. Carving
5. Leather work
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Displays sample or chart showing different art design.
3. Lets pupils identify each of the art.
4. Uses the chart to introduce and explain the meaning of art.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify and listen to the teacher’s explanation.
3. Discuss the the origin of art.
Pupil’s Activities - Discuss the meaning and origin of Art.
4. States the uses of Art.
Pupil’s Activities - Name some uses of Art.
5. Names some Nigerian works of Arts.
Pupil’s Activities - Mention some Nigerian works of Arts.
6. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as instructed.
CONCLUSION
- To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
- Next Lesson Branches of Art Primary 5 (Basic 5) - Cultural and Creative Arts
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to -
1. State the meaning of Art
2. Describe the origin of Arts.
3. List 5 the uses of Art.
4. Name 5 Nigerian works of Art.

topics.title: Fabric Decoration by Tie and Dye Methods: Meaning, Methods, Materials, and How to Produce Tie and Dye | Primary 5 (Basic 5) Third Term Week 4 Cultural and Creative Arts
topics.content:
FABRIC DECORATION BY TIE AND DYE METHODS: MEANING, METHODS, MATERIALS AND HOW TO PRODUCE TIE AND DYE
CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ARTS (CCA)
PRIMARY 5 - THIRD TERM - WEEK 4
THEME -  ARTS AND CRAFTS
PREVIOUS LESSON - Traditional Apprenticeship System: Meaning and Objectives of the Traditional Apprenticeship System and Trades Where Apprenticeship Is Practised | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 6 Cultural and Creative Arts
TOPIC - FABRIC DECORATION BY TIE AND DYE
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Methods of Tie and Dye
3. Materials for Tie and Dye and How to Produce Tie and Dye
4. Importance of Tie and Dye and Safety Precautions
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of tie and dye.
2. Identify the different methods of tie and dye.
3. List the materials used for tie and dye.
4. Describe the steps involved in producing tie and dye.
5. Produce a simple tie and dye pattern using the correct method.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about fabric decoration, card making, mosaic, and weaving.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing tie and dye as another method of decorating fabric with beautiful patterns.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. White cotton fabric
2. Fabric dye
3. Plastic bucket or bowl
5. Water
6. Rubber bands or strings
7. Needle and thread
8. Hand gloves
9. Wooden stick or spoon
10. Apron or old clothes
11. Samples or pictures of tie and dye fabrics
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Have you seen clothes with colourful patterns that look different from ordinary printed fabrics? Some of these beautiful designs are made by tying, folding, twisting, or stitching a piece of cloth before dipping it into dye. This method of decorating fabric is called tie and dye.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of tie and dye, the methods used, the materials required, and the steps involved in producing simple tie and dye designs.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF TIE AND DYE
Tie and dye is a method of decorating fabric by tying, folding, stitching, or twisting parts of the cloth before dipping it into dye. The tied parts resist the dye and create beautiful patterns when untied.
METHODS OF TIE AND DYE
Common tie and dye methods include:
1. Tying method - Parts of the fabric are tied tightly with string or rubber bands before dyeing.
2. Folding method - The fabric is folded into different shapes before dyeing.
3. Stitching method - Parts of the fabric are stitched with thread, pulled tightly, and then dyed.
4. Twisting method - The fabric is twisted into a spiral shape and tied before dyeing.
5. Crumpling method - The fabric is crumpled into a loose ball and tied before dyeing.
MATERIALS FOR TIE AND DYE
The materials needed include:
1. White cotton fabric
2. Fabric dye
3. Water
4. Plastic bucket or bowl
5. Rubber bands or strings
6. Needle and thread (for stitching method)
7. Hand gloves
8. Wooden stick or spoon for stirring
9. Apron or old clothes
LESSON 2 - HOW TO PRODUCE TIE AND DYE
1. Wash and dry the white fabric.
2. Fold, tie, twist, stitch, or crumple the fabric.
3. Prepare the dye according to the instructions.
4. Wear hand gloves before handling the dye.
5. Dip the tied fabric into the dye solution.
6. Leave it for some time so the dye is absorbed.
7. Remove the fabric and allow it to dry.
8. Untie or remove the stitches after drying.
9. Rinse the fabric and dry it again to reveal the design.
IMPORTANCE OF TIE AND DYE
Tie and dye:
1. Produces attractive fabric designs.
2. Promotes creativity.
3. Preserves Nigerian cultural heritage.
4. Can be used to make clothing and household items.
5. Creates employment and income opportunities.
SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
1. Wear hand gloves when handling dye.
2. Work in a well-ventilated area.
3. Avoid spilling dye on the skin or eyes.
4. Wash hands after the activity.
5. Keep dye materials away from food.
LESSON 3 - WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Tie and dye is a method of decorating ______.
A. metal
B. wood
C. glass
D. fabric
2. Which of the following is a method of tie and dye?
A. Tying
B. Sweeping
C. Digging
D. Frying
3. Which material is used to tie the fabric before dyeing?
A. Plate
B. Spoon
C. Rubber band
D. Ruler
4. What is used to colour the fabric?
A. Chalk
B. Fabric dye
C. Sand
D. Flour
5. Which of the following should be worn while handling dye?
A. School tie
B. Hand gloves
C. Hat
D. Socks
B. Fill in the Gaps
Complete the sentences using the words in the box: fabric, dye, tying, gloves, folding
6. Tie and dye is used to decorate ______.
7. The colouring substance used is called ______.
8. ______ is one method of tie and dye.
9. ______ is another method of tie and dye.
10. Hand ______ protect the hands during dyeing.
C. True or False
11. Tie and dye produces beautiful patterns on fabric. ______
12. White cotton fabric can be used for tie and dye. ______
13. Rubber bands can be used to tie the fabric. ______
14. Tie and dye does not require any dye. ______
15. Wearing gloves is not a safety precaution during tie and dye. ______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B
16. Tie and Dye - A. Colours the fabric
17. Fabric dye - B. Protect the hands
18. Rubber band - C. Ties the fabric
19. Hand gloves - D. Decorates fabric
20. Folding - E. Method of tie and dye
ANSWER KEYS
1. D - Fabric
2. A - Tying
3. C - Rubber band
4. B - Fabric dye
5. B - Hand gloves
6. fabric
7. dye
8. tying
9. folding
10. gloves
11. True
12. True
13. True
14. False
15. False
16. D - Decorates fabric
17. A - Colours the fabric
18. C - Ties the fabric
19. B - Protect the hands
20. E - Method of tie and dye
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that tie and dye is a method of decorating fabric by tying, folding, stitching, twisting, or crumpling parts of a cloth before dipping it into dye to create beautiful patterns.
Pupils identified the different methods of tie and dye, including the tying, folding, stitching, twisting, and crumpling methods. They also learned the materials used for tie and dye, such as white cotton fabric, fabric dye, rubber bands or strings, water, buckets, hand gloves, and wooden sticks.
Furthermore, pupils learned the steps involved in producing tie and dye, from preparing the fabric and dye to tying, dyeing, drying, untying, and rinsing the fabric.
Finally, pupils understood the importance of tie and dye as a means of promoting creativity, preserving Nigerian cultural heritage, producing attractive fabric designs, and creating employment opportunities.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction - The teacher displays samples or pictures of tie and dye fabrics and asks pupils to observe the different patterns and colours. The teacher introduces the topic tie and dye.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the fabrics and describe the colours and patterns they see.
Step 2: Meaning of Tie and Dye - The teacher explains that tie and dye is a method of decorating fabric by tying, folding, stitching, twisting, or crumpling parts of the cloth before dipping it into dye.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of tie and dye in their own words.
Step 3: Methods and Materials - The teacher explains the common methods of tie and dye:
- Tying method
- Folding method
- Stitching method
- Twisting method
- Crumpling method
The teacher displays and explains the materials needed, such as white cotton fabric, fabric dye, rubber bands, strings, buckets, water, hand gloves, and wooden sticks.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the methods and materials used for tie and dye.
Step 4: Demonstration of Tie and Dye - The teacher demonstrates the steps involved in producing tie and dye:
- Wash and dry the fabric.
- Tie, fold, stitch, twist, or crumple the fabric.
- Prepare the dye solution.
- Wear hand gloves.
- Dip the fabric into the dye.
- Remove and dry the fabric.
- Untie the fabric and rinse it to reveal the pattern.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the demonstration and ask questions.
Step 5: Practical Activity - The teacher guides pupils to produce a simple tie and dye design using one of the methods demonstrated.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils produce simple tie and dye patterns under the teacher’s supervision.
Step 6: Group Activity - The teacher divides the class into four groups and assigns the following activities:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of tie and dye.
- Group 2: Identify the methods of tie and dye.
- Group 3: List the materials used for tie and dye.
- Group 4: Demonstrate the steps involved in producing tie and dye.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, demonstrate, and present their assigned activities.
Step 7: Lesson Summary - The teacher reviews the meaning, methods, materials, steps, and importance of tie and dye.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation - The teacher asks oral and written questions and observes pupils as they demonstrate the tie and dye process.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the evaluation questions and demonstrate simple tie and dye techniques.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. Explain the meaning of tie and dye.
2. Identify five different methods of tie and dye.
3. List five materials used for tie and dye.
4. Describe five steps involved in producing tie and dye.
5. State at least three safety precautions to observe during tie and dye.
6. Produce a simple tie and dye pattern using the correct method.
